script.text: Good morning! I'm Kelly, and this is your daily lesson for April 2. Today we're exploring two powerful ideas together.
You say 'I'm fine' but your arms are crossed, your jaw is tight, and you won't make eye contact.  Which message is true?  Words are only part of communication—often the smaller part.

Research suggests words carry only about 7% of emotional meaning. Tone of voice carries 38%. Body language carries 55%. We think we communicate with language, but our bodies are doing most of the talking. Micro-expressions are involuntary facial expressions lasting just fractions of a second.  They can reveal emotions people are trying to hide.
Today's wisdom: Here's today's wisdom: True understanding requires attention to what isn't said.  Listen with your eyes.
Now let's take what we learned and put it into practice.
Today's growth challenge is Nonverbal Awareness - Read the Full Message.

Here's your activity: In your next conversation, consciously notice nonverbal signals: posture, eye contact, gestures, tone. Does the body match the words? What information comes through channels other than language? This helps you develop awareness of nonverbal communication.
And here's how today's lessons connect: What you learned about how we understand each other can be applied to nonverbal awareness - read the full message. Practice makes progress.
That's today's lesson. Learn something, grow a little. I'll see you tomorrow with something new. Stay curious!
